title: Variable Scope
learning_outcomes: Explain what variable scope contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: local scope.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Reliable programs represent values deliberately. Variables hold changing values, constants name stable values, and type behavior affects comparisons, conversion, function contracts, and error handling. In this lesson, focus on local scope; then compare it with global scope. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use variable scope when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable programs represent values deliberately. Variables hold changing values, constants name stable values, and type behavior affects comparisons, conversion, function contracts, and error handling. For variable scope, begin with local scope. Also distinguish global scope; global; the $globals array. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
